description: Verify that DUT's ARP Reply echoes the *requester's* sender_hw as its target_hw, even when two consecutive Requests come from different MACs — each Reply must answer the Request that triggered it (RFC 826 §2.4)
approach:
[Objective]
DUT must not 'cache' a single target_hw to use across responses; each Reply's target_hw must echo the sender_hw of the Request that triggered it. This case sends two Requests from different sender MACs and checks that each Reply echoes the correct one.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: Request #1 (sender_mac=MAC-ADDR1, target_ip=DUT IP)
2. (Observation 1) DUT → Tester: Reply #1, target_hw == MAC-ADDR1

3. Tester → DUT: Request #2 (sender_mac=MAC-ADDR2, target_ip=DUT IP)
4. (Observation 2) DUT → Tester: Reply #2, target_hw == MAC-ADDR2

[Pass condition]
Reply #1's target_hw equals MAC-ADDR1 AND Reply #2's target_hw equals MAC-ADDR2.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_wrong_target_hw_1 — Reply #1's target_hw was not MAC-ADDR1
• Fail_wrong_target_hw_2 — Reply #2's target_hw was not MAC-ADDR2 (e.g. still MAC-ADDR1 — cache leak)
• Fail_no_response_1 — Reply #1 missing
• Fail_no_response_2 — Reply #2 missing

verdicts.Pass: Both Replies echoed the corresponding requester's MAC — normal per-Request answering
verdicts.Fail_wrong_target_hw_2: Reply #2's target_hw was not MAC-ADDR2 (cache leaked between responses?)
